title: Internet Technology
part: Part B — Networks and the Internet

blocks.html: After studying this chapter you will be able to:

items.html: explain what the internet is and how it began
use the terms WWW, website, web page, browser, URL, domain name, IP address, DNS and ISP correctly
name different ways of connecting to the internet
use email, search engines and other internet services well
follow rules of online safety and recognise phishing

blocks.html: Definition: The internet is a worldwide network of networks. It connects billions of computers, phones and servers so that they can share information using a common set of rules called TCP/IP.

No single person, company or country owns the internet. Each network that joins it is owned by someone — a telecom company, a university, a government — and they all agree to follow the same protocols.

blocks.html: A search engine finds web pages that match the words you type. Examples: Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo.

items.html: Use specific words: Bihar board class 9 syllabus 2026 is better than syllabus.
Put an exact phrase in quotes: "Analytical Engine" .
Search only one site: site:gov.in scholarship .
Remove a word with a minus sign: jaguar -car .
Check that the source is reliable — prefer government, university and well-known sites.

items.html: Intranet: a private network inside an organisation that uses internet technology but only employees can use it (e.g. a company's staff portal).
Extranet: part of an intranet opened to selected outsiders, such as suppliers or partner schools.
Address bar — type the URL or search words.
Tabs — open several pages in one window (Ctrl + T for a new tab, Ctrl + W to close).
Bookmarks — save useful pages (Ctrl + D).
History — list of pages visited (Ctrl + H).
Refresh — reload the page (F5).
Private / Incognito window — does not save history on that device (Ctrl + Shift + N in Chrome). It does not make you invisible on the internet.
Use strong passwords — at least 12 characters with letters, numbers and symbols. Do not use your name or date of birth. Use a different password for each important account.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) — an OTP or app code is needed along with the password.
Never share an OTP, PIN or password — a bank or government office will never ask for it on a call.

Beware of phishing — fake emails, SMS or websites that pretend to be a bank, a delivery company or a scholarship scheme to steal your details. Check the address carefully; sbi-kyc-update.xyz is not SBI.
Look for HTTPS and the padlock before entering personal or payment details.
Think before you post — photos and posts can stay online for ever.
Report cyber crime — call the national helpline 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in.

blocks.html: Did you know? India records more UPI transactions than any other country. Every one of them is protected by your UPI PIN — which is why you should never enter your PIN to receive money. A PIN is needed only to send money.
Aim: To use a browser, a search engine and email correctly.

items.html: Read a URL. Open your browser and visit any government website ending in .gov.in. Copy its URL into your notebook and label the protocol, domain and path.
Search smartly. Search for Bihar tourism and then for site:gov.in Bihar tourism . Compare the results.
Bookmark. Open the DIKSHA website and bookmark it with Ctrl + D. Find it again in the bookmarks bar.
Write an email. In your email account (or the school's practice account), write a mail to your teacher with the subject Workshop 4 – Your Name. Add a classmate in CC.
Attach a file. Attach the Notepad file from Workshop 2 and send the mail. Check the Sent folder.
Spot the phishing. Your teacher will show five messages. Mark each as genuine or phishing and give one reason.

blocks.html: Record: Write the five most useful keyboard shortcuts for browsers.

items.html: The internet is a worldwide network of networks using TCP/IP; it began as ARPANET in 1969 and came to India in 1995.
The WWW is a collection of linked web pages viewed with a browser.
Each device has an IP address; DNS turns domain names into IP addresses; an ISP provides the connection.
A URL has a protocol, domain and path. HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP.
Email, search, e-learning, e-governance, e-commerce and UPI are key services.
Stay safe: strong passwords, 2FA, never share OTP or PIN, watch for phishing, report on 1930.
